Twelve teams, two pools. The Six Nations sides form the Northern pool; New Zealand, South Africa, Australia, Argentina, Japan and Fiji form the Southern pool. Every team plays the six teams from the other pool — three rounds in the south in July, three in the north in November — then Finals Weekend at Twickenham, 27–29 November, decides every place, with the two pool winners meeting in the final.

Pool tables 4 points for a win · bonus point for four tries, and for losing by seven or fewer

Northern pool

Southern pool

France top the north on 17 points, but England's bonus-point win over Australia lifts them to second — level with Ireland on 15 points and ahead on points difference. South Africa and New Zealand are level on a perfect 20 points in the south — they don't meet in the pool stage, so the final could be a rematch of the pool race.

Finals weekend · Twickenham 27–29 November — pairings set by final pool positions after Round 6
